hint_reasoning: No material hint was given (material_hint null), so verify mode does not apply. The spectrum shows one strong totally symmetric-like mode at 155.3 cm-1 (flat in parallel, zero in crossed) and two in-plane anisotropic modes (299.0 and 352.8 cm-1, parallel twofold). This points to a low-symmetry, in-plane anisotropic layered material. I could not match it to a specific material: the skill's reference library, matcher and curated mode tables are outside the working folder, which I was told not to read. Candidates are class-level only and carry low confidence.

peaks.assignment: unassigned; strongest band, isotropic in parallel
peaks.source: Lorentzian fit of angle-averaged spectrum (analysis/fit_avg.py); per-angle fits (analysis/angle_fit.py). Parallel amplitude 39,300 +- 1,000 at all 18 angles, constant to about 2.5 %; crossed 26 +- 240 (zero).

Fit of angle-averaged spectrum (fwhm 4.3 +- 0.4). Parallel amplitude varies with 180-degree period (maximum near 38 deg, minimum near 128 deg, modulation about 145 %, F-test vs constant p ~ 2e-8). Crossed amplitude is nonzero (mean 3,600 +- 330) and varies from about 0 to 9,000 with no clean twofold or fourfold form; crossed scatter (about 2,500) exceeds empty-region control scatter (about 1,400), so the variation is real.

Fit of angle-averaged spectrum (fwhm 4.6 +- 0.1). Parallel amplitude follows 180-degree period (maximum near 127 deg, minimum near 37 deg; chi2 of twofold fit 26 for 15 dof; F vs constant p ~ 1e-15). Crossed amplitude 346 +- 330, consistent with zero (silent).

Averaged crossed fit centre 354.8 (fwhm 6.4, amplitude 2,070 +- 520, about 4 sigma). Crossed amplitude constant over angle within noise (F-test p = 0.4). Not resolved from the strong 352.8 parallel band, so the parallel contribution cannot be excluded.

limits: Identification is not established. No reference-spectrum match was possible: the skill's reference library, matcher and curated mode tables sit outside the working folder, which I was told not to read. The candidate list is class-level and low-confidence.

Rejected by absence (from memory, not checked against a reference): graphene, MoS2/WS2/MoSe2/WSe2 (no bands in the 380-420 cm-1 range, z < 1 in weak-candidate tests), hBN (no 1366 cm-1 band; window ends at 722), black phosphorus (no bands near 440-470 cm-1, z < 1.6).
Spectral window is 60-722 cm-1. Bands outside it (below 60 or above 722 cm-1) cannot be checked, and many diagnostic modes for layered materials lie there.

No Si or other calibration line is present (suspended sample, no substrate). Absolute positions are uncalibrated; assume a systematic offset of a few tenths of a cm-1 before comparing with literature.

Noise is high: per-point scatter is about 1,200 counts (parallel) and 1,400 (crossed), and about 12-13 % of points in each configuration are exactly zero, i.e. clipped. Clipping biases weak crossed amplitudes upward; treat crossed features near the noise with caution.

Crossed 299 cm-1 has real angular variation but no clean twofold or fourfold form, so its class is 'other'. Parallel 155 cm-1 is constant to about 2.5 %, so 'isotropic_par_only' is a classification, not a precise statement of zero modulation.
The 354.8 cm-1 crossed-only component is about 4 sigma on the averaged spectrum and sits in the wing of the strong 352.8 cm-1 parallel band. Treat it as tentative.

Not reported as peaks: crossed 239 cm-1 (averaged fit 587 +- 293, about 2 sigma); parallel 102, 259, 532, 594, 632 cm-1 and crossed 161, 222, 384, 426, 639 cm-1 (all below about 3 sigma after angle averaging; multiple-testing not corrected).

Single-point outliers at noise level (parallel 311 cm-1 at 100 deg, parallel 587 cm-1 at 110 deg, crossed 102 cm-1 at 60 deg, crossed 360 cm-1 at 80 deg) have no neighbour excess and are not reported as cosmic rays. The 382 cm-1 spike is far (about 29 cm-1) from any band, so its effect on the fitted band amplitudes is negligible, but it was not masked.
Layer number, strain, doping and defect density cannot be determined: no relation was applied, no reference data was accessible, and no thickness or calibration check is possible on this spectrum.
The working-folder name was not used as evidence for the material.
Citations: none. No literature source was consulted, so no reference is cited.
